learning_outcomes.text: Improve the capacity for systematic observation and measurement in the field of Chemistry.
Develop manual skills and dexterity in the laboratory, valuing safety and quality as fundamental elements.
Assume the importance of the scientific method as a procedure to follow in experimental work, in any scientific-technical field.
Provide students of Industrial Engineering degrees with the theoretical and practical knowledge of Chemistry required as a basis for addressing the study of other subjects in their degree.
Provide the necessary chemical foundations that allow future graduates to competently tackle the chemical aspects that arise in their professional activities.
Exert a leveling effect on the chemical knowledge contributed by students, which are very uneven according to their previous training.

syllabus_topics: Concepts and basic calculations in Chemistry
Amount of substance and concept of mole
Laws of chemical combinations and gas laws
Structure of matter and chemical bonding
Periodic properties of elements that explain their bonds
Colligative properties of solutions with non-electrolyte solutes
Colligative properties of solutions with electrolyte solutes
Shift of the equilibrium state in industrial processes
Direct and indirect measurement of reaction enthalpies, Hess's law
Concept of entropy and of Gibbs free energy
Criterion of spontaneity of chemical reactions
Nuclear energy: fission and fusion processes
Liquid-solid phase diagrams of two components
Liquid-liquid phase diagrams of two components
Liquid-vapor phase diagrams of two components
Standard electrode potentials and standard cell potentials
Examples of galvanic cells of industrial interest
Electrolytic cells, examples of industrial interest
Quantitative aspects of electrolysis, Faraday's laws
Water and air as raw materials of industrial interest
Water as an industrial raw material: purification, wastewater treatment, and softening processes
Air as an industrial raw material: separation of the components of air and uses of industrial gases
Industrial processes based on Organic Chemistry
Petroleum refining and derived petrochemical processes
Polymerization processes and polymers of industrial interest
Concept and objective of chemical analysis
Analytical signal and classification of analysis methods
Supreme qualities of chemical analysis: accuracy and representativeness
Examples of chemical sensors of industrial interest

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative and/or eliminatory partial exams
Leveraging practical activities carried out in: classroom, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: In continuous assessment, the final grade comprises a partial exam (40%), a final exam (40%), practical lab activities (10%), and knowledge assessed through practice questionnaires and calculations (10%). The partial exam can be recovered in the final exam if not passed; practical lab activities and knowledge about practice are non-recoverable in the ordinary call but notes are carried over to the extraordinary call. In global assessment, a single exam covers all themes (80%), complemented by questionnaires on practical activities (10%) and knowledge about practice (10%), all of which are recoverable. For extraordinary calls, the exam covers all themes (80%), and previous non-recoverable practical activity scores are applied.
